text: Build the photodiode or high-speed-camera input-to-photon measurement rig on the reference desktop before the V0.5 compositor benchmarks.
Procure power meters and establish the energy-measurement methodology before the V1 battery gates.
Procure an HDR reference display and colorimeter for the V2 HDR gates.
Procure and rack the reference machines per tier with remote power, console and capture, and a scheduler for soak runs.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Run multi-day soak tests on lab hardware covering suspend/resume cycles, generation accumulation, repeated application launches and long compositor uptime, with memory and latency trend alerts.
rationale: Beta users will run the system for weeks and CI otherwise only tests minutes.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Build an input-to-photon latency measurement rig (HID injection plus photodiode or high-speed capture) attached to lab machines and report it as a tracked benchmark.
rationale: §54 lists GUI input-to-photon latency but it cannot be measured in software alone.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Instrument lab machines with external power meters and battery-drain cycles to produce the §54 energy benchmarks per release.
rationale: Energy claims for laptops are unverifiable from software counters alone.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Establish a physical hardware lab holding the §62 reference machines with remote power control, network boot, serial or USB-debug consoles, HDMI/DisplayPort capture, USB device switching, programmable HID input, and Wi-Fi and Bluetooth peer devices.
rationale: GPU, suspend, wireless and peripheral behaviour cannot be validated in QEMU and §55 forbids destabilising hardware support.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Deploy lab scheduling software (LAVA-like or custom) that reserves machines, flashes images, runs jobs and returns results to CI, with automatic recovery of an unbootable machine via firmware boot-order fallback to a known-good generation.
rationale: Without automation the lab becomes a manual queue that CI cannot depend on.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Run GPU conformance (Vulkan CTS, dEQP) and compositor tests nightly on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA lab machines and track pass rates per driver generation.
rationale: §56.1 names GPU drivers the hardest hardware problem and regressions must be caught per vendor.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Automate suspend/resume, hibernate and lid/dock event testing with RTC wake across hundreds of cycles on each laptop reference machine.
rationale: Suspend regressions are the most common laptop failure and appear only under repetition.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Maintain a firmware version matrix for lab machines and test system behaviour before and after vendor firmware updates.
rationale: Firmware changes silently alter ACPI, TPM and boot behaviour that the boot and security stacks depend on.
